Once upon a time, Country Mouse lived in a cosy little hole under an old oak tree, at the edge of a quiet field.
His best friend, Town Mouse, lived far, far away in a big, busy town.
Every morning, Country Mouse sat in the sunshine and listened to the birds.
Tweet, tweet, tweet!
One sunny morning, guess who came to visit?
Town Mouse!
She skipped across the field with her little pink bag.
Country Mouse ran out and gave her a big hug.
Welcome to my home!
said Country Mouse.
Country Mouse set out lunch on a flat stone: seeds, sweet blackberries and a crunchy hazelnut.
Town Mouse had never ever tasted a blackberry before.
Yum, yum, yum!
said Town Mouse.
After lunch, the two friends lay in the long grass and watched the clouds float by.
The wind blew in the grass.
Swish, swish, swish!
But Town Mouse wriggled and wriggled.
It's so quiet here!
Isn't it lovely?
That evening, the sun went down, all pink and gold.
The crickets sang.
Chirp, chirp, chirp!
Your home is lovely, but I love mine,
It's a bit too quiet for me.
Come and stay at my house tomorrow!
Yes, please!
The next morning, the two friends rode to town on the back of the farmer's hay cart, all snug in the soft hay.
The big brown horse pulled them all the way.
Clip-clop, clip-clop, clip-clop!
Town Mouse lived in a tall house, right in the middle of the town.
Her home was a teeny-tiny room behind the kitchen wall, with a round red door just her size.
The family had just finished breakfast.
Town Mouse took Country Mouse up onto the big kitchen table.
Wow!
There were cake crumbs, bits of cheese and some juicy grapes.
Help yourself!
Clatter, clatter, clatter!
The plates rattled in the sink.
The cook was washing up and humming a happy song.
Country Mouse jumped.
What's that noise?
It's only the plates,
Town is always busy!
Then the two friends went into the hall.
Vroom, vroom, vroom!
A big round hoover rolled right past them, all by itself.
Country Mouse put his paws over his ears.
It's only the hoover,
Bang, bang, bang!
The wind was banging the big front door.
Country Mouse jumped so high that his straw hat flew right off his head!
It's only the door,
Country Mouse started to giggle.
Town is a bit too busy for me!
That evening, the two friends sat on the kitchen windowsill and watched the town lights twinkle.
I like it nice and quiet.
And I like it nice and busy!
Then the two friends laughed and laughed.
Ha, ha, ha!
The next morning, Country Mouse rode home on the farmer's hay cart.
Town Mouse waved from the doorstep.
Bye-bye! Come back soon!
You come and visit me too, okay?
That night, Country Mouse curled up in his cosy bed under the old oak tree.
Home, sweet home,
He smiled a sleepy smile and closed his eyes.
Far away in the busy town, Town Mouse snuggled into her own little bed.
Outside her window, the town hummed.
Hum, hum, hum!
Every summer and every winter, the two friends visited each other.
And they stayed best friends for ever and ever.
